svg.title: What USPS pages say about filing a claim: who can file, when to file for damaged or missing contents and for lost items by service, insurance, what to have ready, and what happens after you file.
svg.text: USPS claims
What the USPS pages say
Who can file
The mailer or the addressee. For a lost item
the DMM says whoever has the original receipt
or online label record. Exceptions: USPS
Returns and USPS Ship.
Damaged or missing contents
File immediately; no later than 60 days after
the mailing date.
Lost item (from the mailing date)
Priority Mail Express: no sooner than 7 days,
no later than 60 days. Priority Mail, Ground
Advantage, Insured Mail, COD, Registered Mail:
no sooner than 15 days, no later than 60.
APO/FPO/DPO: from 21, 45 or 75 days, up to
180 days or 1 year.
Insurance
Claims cover insured mail, COD, Registered
Mail with insurance and Priority Mail Express.
Some services include insurance; it need not
be bought separately. A Missing Mail Search
looks for the item; it is not a claim.
Have ready
Tracking or label number, proof of insurance
and proof of value. For damage: photos and a
repair estimate. Keep the packaging.
After you file
Decision usually in 5-10 days; up to 30 for
in-depth claims. Two appeals, 30 days each,
counted from the decision date or from
receiving it; the sources differ. Check the
USPS claims page.
Sources: USPS.com claims page, USPS FAQ (Nov. 6,
No amounts or fees are shown.
